openingMessage: A crisis can be a momentous time for a team to grow — if a leader handles it properly.
openingWhy: When monitors alarmed mid-pull on a separator — gas off an unidentified line at 31 ppm — the crew mustered upwind, counted heads, and escalated. Nobody froze, nobody played hero. A bad moment handled by the numbers is the best training the field ever hands out.
leadershipThought: Disciplined people don't rise to the occasion — they fall back on their systems. When pressure arrives, habits take over. Build the right habits before the pressure gets here.

Positive Observation — Horse Head and Flow Line Removal at Second Location (Energy Isolation)
Back-to-back jobs of the same type can create complacency — re-confirming hold points and controls on the second job, rather than assuming it goes the same as the first, is what keeps routine from becoming risky.

Positive Observation — Horse Head and Flow Line Removal with Full Controls (Energy Isolation)
LOTO confirmation before removing horse heads and flow lines protects against stored energy and residual pressure — document it every time so the control is on record, not just in memory.
